title: Chapter 14 — Final Year Project
description: Forty pages of your own work or ₦25,000 at the back gate. Tamara wants to meet your mother. Dubai has a new car.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Final year. The project. Forty pages, a defence, a supervisor's signature. The back gate sells finished projects for ₦25,000. "Any topic, any department, original or your money back." Nobody has ever got their money back.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Expelled students don't write projects. You come to campus anyway, to help Tamara with hers and to remember what it felt like.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: Your topic: "The Akara Index: Prices at Five Lagos Bus Stops".

options.text: Buy one at the back gate. You're tired.

beats.speaker: drBayo
beats.text: (your supervisor, reading chapter three) Your data is from bus stops. Your writing is from the library. (He smiles.) That's the whole of economics.

variants.text: (your supervisor, reading chapter three) You never came to my reading group. (He reads on.) You didn't need to. This is good work, Mr. Somtochukwu.

beats.speaker: tamara
beats.text: (on the library steps) Somto. Convocation is in two months. I want to meet your mother. Properly. Not at a gate. At her stall, or her house, or wherever she is.

variants.text: (on the library steps) You told me everything in third year. Iyana-Wahala, the pap, all of it. (She smiles.) So when do I meet the woman who makes the akara of the gods?
(on the library steps) You warned me about the town hall. My mother hasn't stopped talking about you. Now I want to meet YOUR mother. Fair is fair.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Saturday. Tamara eats nine akara, burns her tongue on the pap, and argues with Garba about the price of tea. Mama watches her the way she watches dough rise.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Dubai has a Mercedes now. Black. Personalised plate: "DXB". He parks it outside the hostel like a dare.

beats.speaker: dubai
beats.text: Roomie. After convocation, I'm out. Real Dubai. (He looks at the car, then at you.) Something big is coming. Bigger than Brenda. I'll need a clean face.

variants.text: Roomie. You remember Brenda? "Somebody's mother"? (He laughs, badly.) I think about that every time. It doesn't stop me. It just ruins it.
Roomie. You watched me work in first year. You never told anyone. (He taps the car.) Loyalty gets paid. Something big is coming.

beats.title: Final Year Project
beats.summary: Forty pages, honest or bought. A mother introduced, or hidden. A black car parked like a dare. Convocation is coming.
